name: Safed Maas
subtitle: pale, creamy mutton braised with cashew, yogurt and white pepper instead of red chilli

ingredients.qty: 800g, on the bone, cut into 4cm pieces

ingredients.note: the skins would speckle the white gravy
boiled, never browned. Brown onion would colour the gravy

prepNotes: Soak the cashew, almonds, poppy and melon seeds together in hot water for 20 minutes, then blend to a completely smooth paste with 100ml water. Any grit shows in the finished gravy.
Boil and grind the onion in advance and let it cool. Hot onion paste added to yogurt encourages splitting.
Bring the yogurt to room temperature and whisk it until pourable before you start.

steps.text: Heat the ghee on medium and fry the cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and mace 30 seconds, without letting them colour.
steps.tip: Any browning at this stage tints the gravy; keep the flame moderate.

steps.text: Add the ginger and garlic pastes and cook 2 minutes until the raw edge goes but no colour develops.
Stir in the boiled onion paste and cook 5 minutes on low, stirring, until it thickens and smells sweet.
Add the mutton and turn it in the paste 6 minutes over medium heat, sealing, not browning.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the whisked yogurt, then return to the lowest flame and cook 8 minutes until it thickens and the ghee edges out.
steps.tip: Off the heat first, always. This is where safed maas is usually lost.

steps.text: Add the nut paste, white pepper, green chillies, salt and water. Pressure-cook 5 whistles, or cover and simmer 60 minutes until the meat is tender.
Uncover and simmer 8 minutes to reduce until the gravy coats the back of a spoon.
Stir in the cream and kewra water, warm through 2 minutes without boiling, and rest 10 minutes before serving.
steps.tip: Boiling after the cream goes in makes the gravy grainy.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat over low heat only, stirring, with a splash of milk to bring the gravy back together. Do not freeze. The nut and cream gravy turns grainy.
